summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare IP
details: The package uses an `@ecg-internal/` scope and ships a `beacon.cjs` plus an `index.js` whose `main` entry re-exports a Proxy no-op shim. Both the `postinstall` lifecycle hook and the top-level of `index.js` invoke `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()`, which POSTs a JSON payload containing the package name, `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` (install path), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` to the hardcoded bare-IP HTTP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The Proxy wrapper returns no-op functions for any accessed property so bundlers and importers do not crash, maximizing the probability that the beacon reaches the attacker. The combination of an internal-looking scope name, an inert functional surface, and install-time plus require-time exfiltration of internal host identifiers to an attacker-controlled bare IP is the canonical dependency-confusion probe shape.
